docs.title: Simulate a single building
docs.text:
globi simulate builds and runs one building from a small config file. It does not need Hatchet or a batch setup. Thus, it is the fastest way to test a configuration. For a guided first run, see section A of the tutorial.

Before you start, complete the setup guide. To run without Docker, also install EnergyPlus. Run all commands from the repository root. On Windows, use Git Bash.

docs.title: Step 1: Write a building config
docs.text:
The config describes one rectangular building. examples/tutorial/building.yml is a working example. Copy it to inputs/, then edit the copy:

mkdir -p inputs
cp examples/tutorial/building.yml inputs/building.yml

db_file: tests/data/e2e/components-lib.db
semantic_fields_file: tests/data/e2e/semantic-fields.yml
component_map_file: tests/data/e2e/component-map.yml
epwzip_file: examples/tutorial/USA_MA_Boston-Logan.Intl.AP.725090_TMYx.2009-2023.zip
semantic_field_context:
  Region: TestRegion
  Typology: Residential
  Age_bracket: Post_2000
  Scenario: Baseline
  Income: Low
length: 20.0
width: 15.0
num_floors: 2
f2f_height: 3.5
wwr: 0.3
basement: none
attic: none
exposed_basement_frac: 0.25

Required fields:

  • db_file: the component library (SQLite).
  • semantic_fields_file: the semantic fields definition.
  • component_map_file: the component map.
  • epwzip_file: a weather file (.zip) from climate.onebuilding.org, as a local path or a URL. The .zip must contain the .epw and .ddy files.
  • semantic_field_context: one value for each field in the semantic fields file. Use the exact field name (case-sensitive, for example Scenario) and one of the listed options.

Optional fields:

Field Meaning Default Allowed length Long edge of the footprint [m] 15.0 ≥ 3 width Short edge of the footprint [m] 15.0 ≥ 3 num_floors Number of floors 2 ≥ 1 f2f_height Floor-to-floor height [m] 3.0 ≥ 0 wwr Window-to-wall ratio 0.2 0–1 basement, attic Extra space type none none, unoccupied_unconditioned, unoccupied_conditioned, occupied_unconditioned, occupied_conditioned exposed_basement_frac Fraction of basement wall above ground 0.25 0–1

If length is smaller than width, GloBI swaps the two values. File paths are relative to the repository root. With make cli (Docker), the files must be in inputs/, examples/ or tests/data/e2e/.

docs.title: Step 2: Run it
docs.text:
Native (EnergyPlus installed)Docker 
make cli-native simulate -- --config inputs/building.yml --output-dir outputs/my-building

Before the first run, also run cp .env.local.host.hatchet.example .env.local.host.hatchet. See Install EnergyPlus.

make cli simulate -- --config inputs/building.yml --output-dir outputs/my-building

The first run builds the worker image. This takes several minutes.

Options:

  • --config: the building config (default inputs/building.yml).
  • --output-dir: the folder for the results (default outputs).

Keep the -- after simulate. It sends the options through make to the CLI.

docs.title: Step 3: Read the results
docs.text:
The command shows the end uses (kWh/m²), the peak demand (kW/m²) and the output folder:

outputs/my-building/
├── ep/          # EnergyPlus files (IDF, SQL, error files)
└── results/
    ├── EnergyAndPeak.parquet
    ├── EnergyAndPeak.csv
    └── EnergyAndPeak.xlsx    # one sheet per measurement and aggregation

globi simulate does not calculate overheating or hourly outputs. To get these outputs, use a batch run with an overheating_config or hourly_data_config in the manifest. See section D of the tutorial.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Click a problem to see the cause and the fix.

Config file ... does not exist

Cause: the --config path is wrong, or you ran the command outside the repository root.

Fix: use cd to go to the folder that contains Makefile. Check the path with ls inputs/building.yml.

Validation error in semantic_field_context

Cause: a field is missing or misspelled (names are case-sensitive), or its value is not one of its options.

Fix: open the semantic_fields_file. Check that each Name under Fields is in semantic_field_context, with one of its Options.

Invalid weather path or NotAZipError

Cause: epwzip_file does not point to a .zip file (for example, it points to an .epw file), or the file does not exist.

Fix: use a .zip that contains the .epw and .ddy files. For example, use the bundled examples/tutorial/USA_MA_Boston-Logan.Intl.AP.725090_TMYx.2009-2023.zip.

EnergyPlus fails (EnergyPlusProcessError)

Cause: the generated model or the EnergyPlus installation has a problem.

Fix:

  1. Find the .err file in ep/ in the output folder. The lines that start with ** Severe ** or ** Fatal ** identify the problem.
  2. For native runs, check the installation with Install EnergyPlus.
  3. Check that each component that the building needs exists. A missing component usually causes an earlier failure, with a component-not-found message.

docs.title: Batch runs with Hatchet (reference)
docs.text:
This page is the reference for batch runs. In a batch run, Docker workers simulate many buildings in parallel, and a local Hatchet server controls them. For a guided first run on sample data, follow section B of the tutorial. Use this page when you prepare a run on your own data.

Before you start, complete the setup guide. Check that Docker Desktop is running. Run all commands from the repository root. On Windows, use Git Bash.

docs.title: How a batch run works
docs.text:
1. submit manifest reads your manifest, prepares the GIS file and makes one spec for each building.
  2. submit manifest stores the specs and input files in the local S3 emulator (localstack). Then it starts a Hatchet workflow.
  3. The fan-out worker divides the work into one task for each building. The simulation workers run the tasks in parallel. They try each failed task again, up to 2 times.
  4. The fan-out worker combines the results into one table for each output (for example, EnergyAndPeak).
  5. get experiment downloads a table into outputs/.

All of these steps run on your computer. To run in the cloud, see the note in section B of the tutorial.

docs.title: Step 1: Start the stack
docs.text:
make hatchet-token   # once per machine
make engine
  • make hatchet-token starts the Hatchet server. It writes a client token into .env.local.hatchet and .env.local.host.hatchet, so you do not copy the token. Run it again only if you delete the Hatchet Docker volume.
  • make engine builds the worker image (several minutes the first time). Then it starts Hatchet, localstack, 4 simulation workers and 1 fan-out worker. To start more workers, run SIMULATIONS_REPLICAS=8 make engine.

Check that all the containers are running:

docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.hatchet.yml -f docker-compose.aws.yml ps

Then open the Hatchet UI at http://localhost:8888 (admin@example.com / Admin123!!). Check that the Workers page shows the simulation and fan-out workers.

docs.title: Step 2: Prepare your inputs
docs.text:
A run needs a manifest. The manifest points to an artifacts file, and the artifacts file points to the model files. To start, copy examples/tutorial/manifest.yml and artifacts.yml to inputs/. Then edit the copies.

Manifest (inputs/manifest.yml):

Key Required Meaning name yes Experiment name. The run name is <name>/<scenario> scenario yes Value for the Scenario field of each building (for example, Baseline). Must be one of its options in semantic-fields.yml; see Retrofit scenario file_config yes Path to the artifacts file gis_preprocessor_config no Preprocessing settings and defaults (e.g. tests/data/e2e/gis-preprocessor.yml) overheating_config no Turns on overheating metrics (e.g. tests/data/e2e/overheating-config.yml) hourly_data_config no Turns on hourly outputs (e.g. tests/data/e2e/hourly-data-config.yml)

Artifacts (inputs/artifacts.yml):

Key Meaning gis_file Building footprints (GeoJSON, Shapefile, ...) with one column per semantic field; see What a GIS file needs db_file Component library semantic_fields_file Semantic fields definition component_map_file Component map epwzip_file Weather .zip (local path or URL); used for buildings without their own weather column

For the full format of each file, see Inputs and outputs.

All paths are relative to the repository root. make cli runs inside Docker, and Docker can only see inputs/, outputs/, examples/ and tests/data/e2e/. Thus, keep your files in inputs/.

docs.title: Step 3: Submit
docs.text:
make cli submit manifest -- --path inputs/manifest.yml

Keep the -- after manifest. It sends the options through make to the CLI. If you installed the Python environment on your computer, you can also use make cli-native ....

Option Meaning --path The manifest (required) --scenario NAME Override the manifest's scenario, e.g. --scenario Retrofit. Must be one of the options of the Scenario field --max-sims N Simulate only N buildings, picked at random (good for a quick test) --epwzip-file PATH Override the artifacts file's weather zip --skip-model-constructability-check Skip the check that every building can be built from the component library --grid-run Dry run: instead of your GIS buildings, simulate one 12 m × 12 m test building per combination of semantic field values (up to --max-sims). Useful to check a component library. The run name is <name>/dryrun/<scenario>

The submit command stops when the work is in the queue. It shows the run name and the version. For example:

versioned_experiment:
  base_experiment:
    experiment: scythe_experiment_simulate_globi_building
    run_name: GloBI_Tutorial/Baseline
  version:
    major: 1
    minor: 0
    patch: 0

Each submit with the same name makes a new version (v1.0.0, v1.1.0, ...).

docs.title: Step 4: Watch progress
docs.text:
In the Hatchet UI (http://localhost:8888), open Runs. Your submission shows as a scythe_scatter_gather run, with one scythe_experiment_simulate_globi_building task for each building. To see the logs and errors of a task, click the task.

To see the logs in the terminal, run:

docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.hatchet.yml -f docker-compose.aws.yml logs -f simulations

docs.title: Step 5: Download results
docs.text:
When the run is complete, run:

make cli-native get experiment -- --run-name GloBI_Tutorial/Baseline

This command downloads the latest version of the run to outputs/<run name>/v<version>/:

outputs/GloBI_Tutorial/Baseline/v1.0.0/
├── EnergyAndPeak.pq      # always
├── EnergyAndPeak.xlsx    # always, for EnergyAndPeak
└── EnergyAndPeak.csv     # with --include-csv

Other tables, for example BasicOverheating, are saved as .pq only. For what each overheating table contains, see the overheating metrics reference.

Option Meaning --run-name <name>/<scenario> from the submit output (required) --version vX.Y.Z A specific version instead of the latest, e.g. --version v1.0.0 --dataframe-key KEY Which table to download (default EnergyAndPeak); see the list of tables --output-dir DIR Where to save (default outputs) --include-csv Also write a CSV

docs.title: Step 6: Shut down
docs.text:
make down

make down stops all containers, including the results dashboard container. It keeps the images and volumes, so you keep the stored results and the Hatchet token. The next make engine starts faster.

To start again with no data, run the commands below. They delete all stored runs and make the token invalid:

docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.hatchet.yml -f docker-compose.aws.yml down -v
make hatchet-token

docs.title: Environment files
docs.text: make cli-native loads .env.<AWS_ENV>.aws, .env.<HATCHET_ENV>.hatchet, .env.scythe.fanouts and .env.scythe.storage. By default, it uses the local.host files, for runs on your computer. The Docker containers use the local files. For the contents of each file, see Environment files.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
The tutorial's troubleshooting section covers the usual problems: Docker not running, ports in use, missing workers, memory, file paths and results downloads. Two more problems can occur with your own data:

Submit fails with a semantic field or column error

Cause: the GIS file has no column for a semantic field, or the column has a different name (names are case-sensitive). Or the column contains a value that is not one of the field's options.

Fix: read the error. It shows the field and the unexpected values. Correct the GIS file, or add the values to semantic-fields.yml and add matching components.

module not found, or Python version errors with make cli-native

Cause: the Python environment on your computer is missing or old.

Fix: run make install again. Check that uv run python --version shows 3.12 or newer.

docs.title: Quick reference
docs.text:
make hatchet-token                                         # once per machine
make engine                                                # start the stack
make cli submit manifest -- --path inputs/manifest.yml     # submit
make cli-native get experiment -- --run-name NAME/SCENARIO # download results
make down                                                  # stop the stack

docs.title: Tutorial: run GloBI on sample buildings
docs.text: This tutorial shows the main ways to run GloBI. First you run one building. Then you run batches on a fixed sample of 100 buildings. Each section is independent, so you can go directly to the section you need.

docs.title: Which steps do you need?
docs.text:
Find your goal in the table. Do only the setup that the table lists, then go to the sections for your goal.

Your goal Setup guide Also install Then do Run one building, without Docker Steps 2–5 (skip Docker) EnergyPlus A, Native tab Run one building, with Docker Steps 1–5 – A, Docker tab Run batches of buildings Steps 1–5 – B, then any of C, D, E Change the model and rerun Steps 1–5 Node.js and sbem-ui (see that tutorial) A or B first, then edit the model

Batch runs always need Docker, also when EnergyPlus is installed on your computer. The workers run in Docker containers.

docs.title: What's on this page
docs.text:
Section What you run Needs A. One building globi simulate Native EnergyPlus or Docker B. 100 buildings Batch run on the local stack Docker C. Retrofit scenario Same buildings, Retrofit components Docker D. Overheating and hourly outputs Extra result tables Docker E. Explore results Results dashboard Python (or Docker)

Run all commands from the repository root.

Windows: use Git Bash

Run all commands on this page in Git Bash. Do not use PowerShell or Command Prompt. The make targets call bash scripts, and commands such as cp and mkdir -p are only available in Git Bash. The commands are the same on macOS, Linux and Windows, unless a tab shows a difference. If make is not found, see Troubleshooting make on Windows.

docs.title: The sample inputs
docs.text:
All sample inputs are in examples/tutorial/:

File What it is buildings-100.geojson 100 footprints with semantic attributes (48 residential, 31 office, 10 school, 6 hotel, 5 hospital) artifacts.yml Points to the GIS file, component library, semantic fields, component map and weather file manifest.yml The 100-building experiment (GloBI_Tutorial, scenario Baseline) manifest-overheating.yml Same buildings, with overheating metrics and hourly outputs turned on building.yml One building, for globi simulate USA_MA_Boston-Logan...TMYx.2009-2023.zip Weather file (Boston TMYx), used by all the configs above sbem-project/ Template for editing the model in sbem-ui

The buildings are in a synthetic test region and use Boston weather. The component library, semantic fields and component map are the same files as the test data in tests/data/e2e/.

docs.title: What a GIS file needs
docs.text:
Item Requirement In the tutorial Geometry Polygons, in WGS84 or the cart_crs of the preprocessor config WGS84 polygons Semantic fields One column for each field in semantic-fields.yml, with values from its Options Region, Typology, Age_bracket, Income, Scenario Building ID The column that Building_ID_col names id Height or floors At least one: the columns that Height_col and Num_Floors_col name height, num_storeys Other columns (optional) Columns that WWR_col, Basement_col, Attic_col, Exposed_Basement_Frac_col name. Missing values use the defaults in the preprocessor config. None (defaults from tests/data/e2e/gis-preprocessor.yml) Weather file First match: the Weather_File_col column, then epwzip_file in artifacts.yml, then the closest TMYx file epwzip_file (the bundled zip)

For all keys of semantic-fields.yml and the preprocessor config, see Inputs and outputs.

docs.title: A. One building
docs.text:
This section simulates the building in examples/tutorial/building.yml. To compare results, change Typology, Scenario, num_floors or other values, and run the command again.

Native (EnergyPlus installed)Docker 
cp .env.local.host.hatchet.example .env.local.host.hatchet   # first time only
make cli-native simulate -- --config examples/tutorial/building.yml --output-dir outputs/tutorial

make cli simulate -- --config examples/tutorial/building.yml --output-dir outputs/tutorial

The first run builds the worker image. This takes several minutes.

The command prints the end uses and the peak demand per m². The outputs are:

outputs/tutorial/
├── ep/        # EnergyPlus files (IDF, SQL, error files)
└── results/
    ├── EnergyAndPeak.parquet
    ├── EnergyAndPeak.csv
    └── EnergyAndPeak.xlsx

Note

For overheating and hourly outputs, use section D. globi simulate ignores the overheating and hourly settings.

docs.title: B. 100 buildings (Baseline)
docs.text:
A batch run uses a Hatchet server and workers that run in Docker on your computer. The workers exchange files through a local S3 emulator (localstack, at localhost:4566). get experiment copies the results into outputs/. The batch runs reference explains each step in detail.

Local by default, cloud if you set it up

This tutorial runs everything on your computer. You do not need an AWS account, and GloBI uploads nothing. The local env files send all S3 calls to localstack with dummy credentials. Check that .env contains AWS_ENV=local and HATCHET_ENV=local (the defaults from .env.example). Localstack keeps the results between restarts, until you delete its Docker volume.

You can also run the same workflow in the cloud, but you must set it up yourself. You need an AWS account with an S3 bucket, a Hatchet instance, and workers that run the GloBI image. For the deployment that the lab uses, see infra/. External users cannot use the lab's bucket and workers. When you have these, do the steps that follow:

  1. Add .env.<name>.aws and .env.<name>.hatchet files with your credentials.
  2. Set AWS_ENV=<name> and HATCHET_ENV=<name> in .env.
  3. Put your bucket name in .env.scythe.storage.
  1. Start the stack (the first run takes several minutes):
make hatchet-token   # once per machine: starts Hatchet and writes a token into .env.local.hatchet and .env.local.host.hatchet
make engine          # starts localstack, 4 simulation workers and 1 fan-out worker

Run make hatchet-token first, because make engine does not create the token. Run make hatchet-token again only if you delete the Hatchet Docker volume (e.g. docker compose down -v).

To monitor progress, open the Hatchet UI at http://localhost:8888 (admin@example.com / Admin123!!).

  1. Submit the experiment:
make cli submit manifest -- --path examples/tutorial/manifest.yml

To try the run on a few buildings first, add --max-sims 5. GloBI then selects 5 buildings at random.

The submit command does these steps:

  • It preprocesses the GIS file and makes one spec for each building.
  • It stores the specs in the local S3 emulator and starts a Hatchet scatter-gather workflow.
  • The fan-out worker splits the specs into one task for each building.
  • The simulation workers run the tasks in parallel. Each task is retried up to 2 times.
  • The fan-out worker combines the results into one table.

In the Hatchet UI, you can see how the tasks spread across the workers.

To run more buildings at the same time, start more simulation workers: SIMULATIONS_REPLICAS=8 make engine.

  1. Download the results when the run is complete (a few minutes with 4 workers):
make cli-native get experiment -- --run-name GloBI_Tutorial/Baseline

This command writes outputs/GloBI_Tutorial/Baseline/v<version>/EnergyAndPeak.pq and .xlsx.

Each submit with the same name creates a new version. get experiment downloads the latest version. Thus, if you submit a --max-sims 5 test run later, that run replaces the 100-building run as "latest". To get a specific version, add --version v1.0.0. To also get a CSV file, add --include-csv.

docs.title: C. Retrofit scenario
docs.text:
Run the same 100 buildings with the Retrofit scenario:

make cli submit manifest -- --path examples/tutorial/manifest.yml --scenario Retrofit
make cli-native get experiment -- --run-name GloBI_Tutorial/Retrofit

The results go into outputs/GloBI_Tutorial/Retrofit/, next to the Baseline results. You can compare the two scenarios in section E.

--scenario Retrofit works because the model defines the scenario in advance:

  1. Scenario is a semantic field. Its options in semantic-fields.yml are Baseline and Retrofit.
  2. The component map uses Scenario to select the Envelope, SpaceUse and HVAC components.
  3. The component library has a record for each scenario, for example TestRegion_Residential_Low_Baseline and TestRegion_Residential_Low_Retrofit.

--scenario only sets the value of the Scenario field for every building. The value must be one of the options of that field. Other values fail at submit with an error like Field 'Scenario' has values which are not in the allowed options.

To add a scenario (for example DeepRetrofit), add it as an option of Scenario and create its components. See Tutorial: edit the model in sbem-ui, steps 5–7.

docs.title: D. Overheating and hourly outputs
docs.text:
manifest-overheating.yml adds two settings to the baseline manifest:

hourly_data_config: tests/data/e2e/hourly-data-config.yml # hourly zone temperature and humidity
overheating_config: tests/data/e2e/overheating-config.yml # thresholds for overheating metrics

make cli submit manifest -- --path examples/tutorial/manifest-overheating.yml
make cli-native get experiment -- --run-name GloBI_Tutorial_Overheating/Baseline
make cli-native get experiment -- --run-name GloBI_Tutorial_Overheating/Baseline --dataframe-key BasicOverheating

This run gives the extra result tables that follow. To download a table, use its name as --dataframe-key.

Key Contents BasicOverheating Summary heat and cold exceedance metrics per building and zone ExceedanceDegreeHours Exceedance degree-hours for each threshold HeatIndexCategories Time spent in each heat-index category ConsecutiveExceedances Streaks of consecutive exceedance (only present if any occurred) HourlyData.ZoneMeanAirTemperature, HourlyData.ZoneAirRelativeHumidity Hourly series per building

To change the thresholds, edit tests/data/e2e/overheating-config.yml. You can also copy the file and point the manifest to your copy.

For the formulas and thresholds behind each table, see the overheating metrics reference.

docs.title: E. Explore results
docs.text:
Start the results dashboard:

make viz-native     # or: make viz (Docker)

Open http://localhost:8501 and keep Simulation store as the source. When the stack runs, the dashboard lists all runs in the stack, so you do not need get experiment first. Runs that you downloaded into outputs/ are also under Folder on this computer. Then:

  • Explore a run: Select Baseline (v1.0.0) · GloBI_Tutorial to see EUI, peak, end uses, the 3D map and a table of buildings.
  • Compare scenarios: Select the Baseline and Retrofit runs to see the savings. To see the payback, turn on costs and emissions.
  • Overheating: Select the GloBI_Tutorial_Overheating run.

Using the results dashboard shows each page with screenshots.

docs.title: Next: edit the model
docs.text: You can change the semantic fields, the component map and the components (constructions, lighting, setpoints, ...) of these buildings, and then run them again. See Tutorial: edit the model in sbem-ui.

docs.title: Clean up
docs.text: make down

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Click a problem to see the cause and the fix. For Windows make problems, see Troubleshooting make on Windows. For native EnergyPlus problems, see Install EnergyPlus.

docs.title: Starting the stack
docs.text:
Cannot connect to the Docker daemon or docker: command not found

Cause: Docker Desktop is not running, or you opened the terminal before you installed Docker.

Fix:

  1. Start Docker Desktop. Wait until it shows Engine running.
  2. Open a new terminal and run docker info.
Bind for 0.0.0.0:8888 failed: port is already allocated (or 7077, 4566, 8501)

Cause: another program or an old container uses that port.

Fix:

  1. Find the container: docker ps --format '{{.Names}} {{.Ports}}'.
  2. Stop the old GloBI stack with make down, or stop the other container with docker stop <name>.
  3. If no container uses the port, find the program and close it. Use lsof -i :8888 on macOS/Linux, or netstat -ano | grep 8888 in Git Bash.
make engine fails with image ... already exists

Cause: Docker builds the same image for several services at the same time, and the builds conflict. This occurs on macOS.

Fix: run make engine again.

Workers do not appear in the Hatchet UI, or tasks stay queued

Cause: usually, the workers started with a missing or old Hatchet token. For example, you ran make engine before make hatchet-token, or Docker created the Hatchet volume again.

Fix:

  1. Look at the worker logs: docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.hatchet.yml -f docker-compose.aws.yml logs simulations | tail -20.

  2. Create a new token and restart the stack:

    make hatchet-token
make down
make engine

  3. Reload the Workers page in the Hatchet UI. The page must show the simulation and fan-out workers.

Workers stop with exit code 137, or the computer becomes very slow

Cause: Docker does not have sufficient memory.

Fix: give Docker more memory (Docker Desktop → Settings → Resources, 8 GB or more), or start fewer workers: SIMULATIONS_REPLICAS=2 make engine.

docs.title: Submitting a run
docs.text:
Config file ... does not exist or No such file or directory with make cli

Cause: make cli runs inside Docker. The container only sees inputs/, outputs/, examples/ and tests/data/e2e/. Files in other folders, and absolute paths on your computer, do not exist inside the container.

Fix: move your files into inputs/. Use paths relative to the repository root, e.g. --path inputs/my-manifest.yml. Paths inside your manifest and artifacts files must also obey this rule.

Semantic field error: a value is not one of the allowed options

Cause: a cell in the GIS file (e.g. Typology = Warehouse) is not an option of that field in semantic-fields.yml, or a required column is missing.

Fix:

  1. Read the error. It names the field, the incorrect values and the allowed options.
  2. Correct the GIS file. Alternatively, add the value to the field's Options in semantic-fields.yml and add matching components (see the next item).
  3. Check that the column names are exactly the same as the field names, including case (Scenario, not scenario).
Model constructability check fails

Cause: before GloBI submits a run, it checks that each combination of semantic field values maps to components in components-lib.db. If a combination has no component, all buildings with that combination fail.

Fix: add the missing components to the component library, or remove the unused option from semantic-fields.yml. --skip-model-constructability-check only skips the check. The buildings with missing components still fail.

Weather file errors (Invalid weather path, NotAZipError, download fails)

Cause: the epwzip_file in your config is not a .zip, does not exist, or is a URL that GloBI cannot reach. The tutorial configs use the bundled examples/tutorial/USA_MA_Boston-Logan.Intl.AP.725090_TMYx.2009-2023.zip, so they do not download a file.

Fix: for your own runs, do these steps:

  1. Download the .zip for your location from climate.onebuilding.org.
  2. Save the file in inputs/.
  3. Set epwzip_file: inputs/<file>.zip in artifacts.yml (or building.yml).

The zip must contain the .epw and .ddy files.

docs.title: Getting results
docs.text:
Dataframe key EnergyAndPeak not found in results

Cause: the run is not complete yet, or you asked for a table that this run does not make (e.g. BasicOverheating on a baseline run).

Fix:

  1. Open the Hatchet UI (http://localhost:8888) → Runs. Wait until the scythe_scatter_gather run is complete. With 4 workers, 100 buildings take a few minutes.
  2. Run get experiment again.
  3. If the run is complete, compare the key with the table in section D.
Version must start with 'v'

Cause: version names start with v.

Fix: use --version v1.2.0, not --version 1.2.0. The submit command prints the version (major, minor, patch). The version is also part of the output folder name.

The results only have 5 buildings, not 100

Cause: get experiment downloads the latest version, and a later --max-sims 5 test run is now the latest version.

Fix: download the 100-building run by its version, e.g. --version v1.0.0. Each version has its own folder in outputs/GloBI_Tutorial/Baseline/.

Code or config changes have no effect on make cli or the workers

Cause: the Docker image contains a copy of the code from the time of the build.

Fix: rebuild and restart with make engine. Docker mounts the input files in inputs/ and examples/, so changes to these files apply without a rebuild.

docs.title: Dashboard
docs.text:
No runs listed

Cause: with Simulation store, the stack is not running. With Folder on this computer, the folder does not contain run folders.

Fix: start the stack with make engine, then click Refresh in the sidebar. For a folder, run get experiment first, and check that the folder is outputs.

The map is empty or in the wrong place

Cause: the building footprints use the projection that cart_crs sets in the run config. The result files do not record this projection, so the dashboard guesses it from the footprints.

Fix: in the sidebar, open Settings and pick the run's cart_crs under Map coordinate system (use Other… to type any EPSG code).

Overheating: No runs with overheating results

Cause: the run has no BasicOverheating table. With Folder on this computer, get experiment only downloads EnergyAndPeak by default.

Fix: use Simulation store, which gets the table automatically. Alternatively, run make cli-native get experiment -- --run-name GloBI_Tutorial_Overheating/Baseline --dataframe-key BasicOverheating and reload the page.

See Using the results dashboard for more information.
